content.text: A **truth tree** tests an argument by searching for a counterexample. Write the premises and the denied conclusion, then break the formulas apart.
P ∧ Q adds P and Q to the branch. P ∨ Q splits the branch in two. A branch that holds a formula and its denial closes. If every branch closes, the argument is valid.

examples.title: The rules
lines: A ∧ B: write A and B on the branch.
A ∨ B: split into A and B.
A → B: split into ¬A and B.

examples.title: A closed tree
lines: Test P → Q, P, so Q.
P → Q splits into ¬P and Q.
¬P closes against P. Q closes against ¬Q.
examples.conclusion: Every branch closes, so the argument is valid.

question.prompt: What does a closed branch mean?
question.hint: A closed branch holds a formula and its denial.
question.explanation: A branch with both P and ¬P describes an impossible case. If every branch closes, there is no counterexample.
